text:
mia.security: heads-up — we need to finalize the key rotation approach for customer-envelope keys this quarter. automatic KMS rotation vs manual rewrap? thoughts?

sam.ops: +1 to discussing. main constraint is backwards compatibility for older ciphertexts and SDKs that call our decrypt path. automatic rotation (CMK auto-rotate) doesn't rewrap existing DEKs, only rotates the key material — ciphertexts tied to old key versions still decrypt via KMS but we need to ensure latency and error patterns stay stable.

jin.prodeng: agree. also need to think about on-disk cache of DEKs in the runtime. If we rotate CMK and KMS starts returning new ciphertexts for DEK rewraps we must flush caches gracefully.

alice.audit: from compliance side, key policy changes and rotation events must be auditable. we need structured audit logs that include: key_id, principal, rotation_type (auto/manual), and rollout cohort. Also retain logs for 7 years for regulated customers.

kms-bot: Notice: scheduled rotation window for alias/prod-envelope-key in 3 days (maintenance window: 2025-05-01T02:00Z - 04:00Z). Use `--force` for immediate rewrap operations.

mia.security: good point on logs. For the technical approach i'm leaning toward a hybrid: enable CMK automatic annual rotation for crypto hygiene, but implement a controlled rewrap pipeline for DEKs so we can do staged rollouts and rewrap metadata. Automatic CMK rotation is low-effort but doesn't help us move ciphertexts to new envelope keys on our schedule.

sam.ops: hybrid makes sense. proposed steps: 1) add a rewrap API that re-encrypts DEKs under new CMK alias; 2) run canary rewrap on 1% of objects, monitor decrypt errors & latencies for 48h; 3) expand to 10%, then 50%, then full. Have rollback path to rewrap back to previous key if we see regression.

jin.prodeng: need implementation details — rewrap should be idempotent and support concurrency. sample AWS re-encrypt command for batch job:
```
aws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://old_dek.ct \
  --source-encryption-context Application=redwood \
  --destination-key-id alias/prod-envelope-key-v2 \
  --destination-encryption-context Application=redwood \
  --output text > new_dek.ct
```
We should also add a server-side job that calls Encrypt with the new CMK and swaps pointers atomically.

alice.audit: make sure every rewrap action writes an audit entry to our central audit log with old_key_version, new_key_version, requester, and object_id. Also record IAM role used for the rewrap.

sam.ops: GCP note: Cloud KMS rotation is similar but key versions are explicit. our rewrap job for GCP should call `gcloud kms keys versions create --key` to create a new version and then use `gcloud kms encrypt` with the new version. For Azure Key Vault the flow is rotate key + re-encrypt DEKs via `az keyvault key rotate` + rewrap step. Need vendor-specific adapter in the rewrap service.

mia.security: question about encrypted backups and old versions — do we rewrap historical backups? or leave cold storage alone and document that older backups decrypt with previous key versions?

jin.prodeng: i'd prefer not touching immutable backups unless a customer requests it. For our hot store & customer-facing data we rewrap. Cold archived blobs we can leave as-is but surface a note in the audit and support docs.

sam.ops: operational concerns: rate limits with KMS. rewrap at scale will hit requests/sec caps. plan to implement throttled workers with exponential backoff and token-bucket. also run in cross-region mode to minimize latency and spread quota.

alice.audit: RBAC: only ops-runner and security-rotation-role should be allowed to call the rewrap API. require MFA and temporary session tokens (sts) for the rotation run. record the role session name in audit logs.

mia.security: test matrix before rollout: 1) unit tests for rewrap logic; 2) integration in staging with sample customer data; 3) canary in production on low-risk namespace; 4) run chaos test that simulates KMS throttling and nodal failure.

kms-bot: Tip: when re-encrypting, preserve EncryptionContext fields exactly — mismatch will cause decrypt failures.

jin.prodeng: agree, encryption context must be preserved. we'll add strict validation and a small helper lib that asserts equality before swap.

sam.ops: proposed timeline: start staging run next Tue, canary the following week (10% for 48h), expand over 2 weeks if no regressions. full completion target: end of quarter.

alice.audit: add separate schedule for enterprise customers who require longer notice (30 days) and allow opt-out window. we should surface a support banner and send emails.

mia.security: ownership: sam.ops owns rewrap service and runbook, jin.prodeng owns runtime cache changes, alice.audit owns logging retention & customer notices. i'll own the rollout policy and gates.

sam.ops: I'll seed the PR with the rewrap worker and quotas. Quick question: do we want to store both old and new DEKs during transition to allow immediate rollback? that increases storage but simplifies rollback.

jin.prodeng: store both as optional fields with TTL of 14 days. That gives rollback window and we can garbage collect afterwards.

alice.audit: ensure garbage collection also logs deletion events (object_id, key_version_deleted, who_triggered). retention policy must be documented.

mia.security: ok — sounds like consensus. action items: sam open PR + runbook, jin add cache flush & helper lib, alice publish audit spec and customer notice draft. We'll reconvene after staging run. :thumbsup:

sam.ops: on it.

jin.prodeng: adding tests now.

alice.audit: drafting notice.

kms-bot: Scheduled task created: rotation-rewrap-job-1755004321, initial canary at 2025-05-08T10:00:00Z.
